record.paper_title: Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics
record.context_brief: New examples of compact Hessian manifolds
record.original_question: Construct examples of compact Hessian manifolds other than direct products of hyperbolic compact Hessian manifolds and flat compact Hessian manifolds. In particular, beyond the known example of a compact Hessian manifold with a nontrivial fiber bundle structure whose base is hyperbolic and whose fiber is flat, can one construct an example having no fiber bundle structure, perhaps by using deformation theory of affine structures?

evidence.quote: Construct examples of compact Hessian manifolds other than direct products of hyperbolic compact Hessian manifolds and flat compact Hessian manifolds. As one of them, we have a compact Hessian manifold admitting a non-trivial fiber bundle structure whose base space is a hyperbolic compact Hessian manifold and whose fiber is a flat compact Hessian manifold, which is constructed in a similar method to that of the construction of Kuga's fiber varieties in the theory of automorphic functions (cf. [8]). Can one construct another example with no fiber bundle structure by using the deformation theory of affine structures?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Hessian manifold is a flat affine manifold $(M,\nabla)$ equipped with a Riemannian metric $g$ such that, locally with respect to affine coordinates $x^1,\dots,x^n$ in which $\nabla$ is the standard flat connection, there exists a smooth function $\varphi$ with $g_{ij}=\partial^2\varphi/\partial x^i\partial x^j$. A compact Hessian manifold is called flat if its Hessian metric is flat, and hyperbolic if the Koszul form $\alpha=D\log\det(g_{ij})$ (where $D$ denotes the affine connection) defines a Hessian metric $D\alpha$ that is positive definite. 

Two classes of compact Hessian manifolds are known: hyperbolic compact Hessian manifolds and flat compact Hessian manifolds, together with their direct products. A further class is provided by total spaces of nontrivial fiber bundles whose base is a hyperbolic compact Hessian manifold and whose fiber is a flat compact Hessian manifold (constructed in analogy with Kuga's fiber varieties).

Problem. Construct compact Hessian manifolds that are not of any of the above types. In particular, exhibit a compact Hessian manifold which admits no nontrivial fiber bundle structure of the above kind and is not a direct product of a hyperbolic and a flat compact Hessian manifold, possibly by employing the deformation theory of affine structures.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on the geometry and topology of compact Hessian manifolds (e.g., 3-dimensional classifications and constructions of Koszul-type families with negative scalar curvature) has produced new examples beyond products and the Kuga-type fiber bundles, but it is not clearly documented that the specific question — constructing a compact Hessian manifold which admits no such fiber bundle structure and is not a product, via deformation of affine structures — has been definitively resolved. Status remains unclear from available sources.

status_evidence.title: On Topology and Geometry of Hessian Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Curved compact orientable Hessian manifolds must be mapping tori; non-trivial families of compact Hessian manifolds of Koszul type with negative scalar curvature have been constructed.
status_evidence.claim: New non-product examples of compact Hessian manifolds exist, but the precise question is not clearly resolved.

status_evidence.title: The Topology of 3-Dimensional Hessian Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of compact orientable 3-dimensional Hessian manifolds includes Hantzsche–Wendt manifolds, Seifert fibered spaces, and (H^2 x R)/Gamma quotients.
status_evidence.claim: Examples of compact Hessian manifolds beyond direct products are known in low dimensions.
